study: Scalp, forearm and wrist measurements during cued two-axis pointing
question: On a previously examined exploratory group, does adding forearm muscle activity improve the shared Transformer's forecast of the two measured wrist angles 250 ms later on the stored clock? Does scalp EEG add anything beyond forearm EMG?
source: Jorge German Perez Blanco and Javier Mauricio Anteliz Ortiz, EEG-EMG-WristMotion Dataset, Figshare v3, doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.29666735.v3, CC BY 4.0.

roles.selection: Whole-person roles were assigned before individual data were read. Only task blocks 1 to 8 corresponding to source runs 03 to 10 were eligible. One training run was absent and one recorded trial failed the common validity mask. Baseline and unpaired acquisitions were excluded. All six windows of one previously published example trial were removed from development recipients and donors.

row: Each run provides cue and return marker indices, aligned EEG/forearm EDF and independently verified encoder columns. Preserve the original person/block/trial/slot identifiers. On the 512 Hz stored grid, use six target offsets 384,512,640,768,896,1024 after cue. History is 256 stored ticks ending 128 ticks before each target, pooled into 16 nonoverlapping 16-tick bins. Preserve the prior common full-trial finite/support mask. Independently index target angle rows and event identities from pinned angle arrays and trial markers, and require exact agreement with extractor labels. Source cue-relative time avoids absolute run time as an extra predictor. The source reports 100 Hz nominal encoder refresh and unmeasured instrument delay.
inputs: All fits see the same two anchor-relative mean encoder angles per bin, measured final absolute two-axis anchor (TRAIN-standardized) and six one-hot positions after the visual cue. No direction, identity or encoded natural language. Motion + EMG adds 4 RMS bipolar L-minus-R channel differences per bin (stored microvolts). Motion + EMG + EEG adds 8 measured scalp channel means (stored microvolts). Every time-dependent feature is available by cutoff, including the anchor in each relative angle bin. The output is encoder change from anchor, added back before scoring. No neural origin, synaptic signal, sensation or force is observed.
fit: Only three fresh shared HandArmLearner fits, each using the same complete TRAIN support, model topology/seed and row order. Keep the prior ridge weights and TRAIN-only z-scores of inputs, anchor and target residual from the November 19 muscle study. Never refit ridge, prior temporal CNN, or prior corrections. The fixed Transformer uses width 24, four heads, one temporal layer, FF width 48, dropout 0, Gaussian NLL with log variance bounds [-6,6], float32, seed 20261120. Train four complete epochs, permuting all eligible examples with NumPy default_rng(20261120) once per fit, batch size 96, AdamW lr .001, betas [.9,.999], epsilon 1e-8, decay .01, gradient norm 1. All groups enabled, paired aligned_forecast_step. Row-weighted learner and participant-weighted published ridge are distinct fitted systems. No tuning, warm-start, refitting, DEV model selection or early stopping.
controls: Frozen motion-only / motion+EMG / motion+EMG+EEG ridge weights read the same rows and features. Also report persistence, previous frozen motion-only CNN ensemble, linear extrapolation and TRAIN timing. Use original next eligible trial in same person/block and target slot with wrap. Run aligned and rotated EMG through the same EMG model, and aligned and rotated EEG through the same full model, on both Transformer and ridge. Keep anchor, motion, cue, target and non-rotated streams fixed. Record no-cross-block bijection, singleton/donor count and private donor/receiver provenance. These controls break the pairing, not possible shared movement artifacts.
outcomes: Equal participant mean of per-axis mean squared error, then square root, degrees. Primary paired contrast: Transformer motion+EMG minus Transformer motion-only. Prespecified secondary contrasts: full minus motion+EMG, aligned minus each rotated stream, each Transformer versus same-information ridge and versus persistence; frozen motion CNN for context. Also report each axis, each participant privately, leave-one-person-out range for primary/EEG/controls and descriptive 95% marginal Gaussian interval coverage and mean widths per model/axis. No threshold, significance, population, new-cohort confirmation or live interpretation. Report all outcomes even for poorer models.
runtime: One CPU process with one PyTorch intra-op thread and one inter-op thread, float32, deterministic algorithms, one BLAS thread. PyTorch 2.14.1+cpu, NumPy 2.4.6, Python 3.13.15 on Linux.
